newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA FINMIN TO HIT C.BANK LOAN LIMIT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA FINMIN TO HIT C.BANK LOAN LIMIT.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry has almost used up this year's funds earmarked for direct borrowing from the central bank (BNB) with the latest six billion lev loan approved by the BNB, figures showed.

The BNB said late on Thursday it has decided to lend the Finance Ministry a three-month loan worth 6.0 billion levs at an interest equal to BNB's main interest rate, now set at 25 percent monthly or 300 percent annually.
With this loan the ministry's direct debt to the BNB to rises to 24.539 billion levs, just 200 million levs below the annual limit in this year's consolidated budget.

Under the budget frame the direct loans from the central bank to the ministry cannot exceed five percent of the revenue target set for the 1996 consolidated government budget or 24.739 billion levs, BNB board member Nikolina Micheva told Reuters.
This means that the ministry cannot directly borrow more than 200 million levs from the BNB before it covered at least a part of its debt, another BNB official said.

Under latest budget law provisions, the BNB is obliged to buy treasury paper isued by the finance ministry, which has remained undersubscribed in auctions. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
